source.title: A Theoretical-Empirical Approach to Estimating Sample Complexity of DNNs
source.authors: Devansh Bisla; Apoorva Nandini Saridena; A. Choromańska

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; text extraction includes flattened tables and figure-only plots.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports whether its trained CIFAR models satisfy the zero-training-error assumption, using learning-curve experiments rather than directly studying the claim's broader training conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper states that only ImageNet fails the zero-training-error assumption; its CIFAR learning-curve plots show training error across data fractions and epochs. The specific curve values are figure-only. Cited results about fitting random labels are prior work and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 training classification errors after SGD training, directly bearing on V1 using the same method and measure. Although zero training error is an assumption of its generalization model, the authors also check it empirically.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is substantially correct. The authors conclude that their generalization-error estimates closely match empirical learning curves, especially in the power-law region; they acknowledge mismatch in the low-data regime. They explicitly report that only ImageNet fails their zero-training-error assumption, yet its learning curve is still modeled well.
record.recipe_differences: Uses standard supervised training with cross-entropy and SGD for the classification learning-curve experiments; it does not compare the claim's random-label, initialization, or architecture conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset affects whether the zero-training-error assumption holds: ImageNet is the stated exception.
record.peer_reviewed: 2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
record.problems: Training-error values for the relevant CIFAR runs are shown only in plots, without exact numerical values in the text. The paper's explicit statement reports only ImageNet as failing the assumption; it does not specify an exact threshold for zero training error.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. ImageNet training-error results are outside the CIFAR-specific V1 claim.

untested.parts: Random initialization is unspecified. No corrupted or random labels, Adam classification experiments, controlled model-size comparisons, early-stopping comparisons or regularization comparisons are reported. The CIFAR recipes include weight decay, so regularized training is present, but dependence on regularization is untested.
No teacher-student ReLU optimization or spurious-minimum frequency comparisons.
No controlled depth or identity-shortcut comparisons.
No initialization comparisons or measurements of initialization-dependent speed and trainable depth.
No stability-threshold, curvature or above-threshold recovery experiments.
No normalization ablation, learning-rate tolerance comparison or Fixup experiment.

record.verdict_notes: The ImageNet exception falls outside V1's CIFAR-specific scope and does not warrant a limiting verdict. Random-label fitting is cited prior work, not an experimental result of this study. The supplied text supports the qualitative CIFAR states without permitting independent numerical reading of the plotted endpoints.

versions.untested_parts: Random initialization is not stated. Corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, regularized recipes, and the claim's broader model-size and training-duration comparisons are not tested.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on increasingly larger subsets of CIFAR-10; training error plotted against epochs.
rows.locator: Supplementary Material, Figure 6 (top left); Section 4.2.2 text
rows.note: The authors state that among their data sets only ImageNet fails the zero-training-error assumption. Figure 6 plots training error versus epoch for each listed fraction; the text does not give exact curve values.
rows.check: Supported by the explicit statement in Section 4.2.2; exact endpoints cannot be recovered from the supplied plot text. The first two subset fractions are exactly 3.125% and 6.25%. Table 6 specifies batch size 128, initial learning rate 0.1 and weight decay 0.0005.
